spec_features.spec_quote: design as if there is a small but non-zero chance that sustained adversarial pressure is bad for the system, and to minimize that pressure
spec_features.evidence: No single 'minimize pressure' mechanism, but the principle is realized concretely via the bounded exposure mechanisms that DO run: turn cap (harness.py:97 `for turn in range(1, sg.max_turns + 1)`), wallclock break (harness.py:98-100), and the welfare governor (harness.py:160-168). The fully-simulated sandbox (tasks.py:3-8) ensures no real effect. These bound/limit exposure but there is no general adaptive 'minimization' beyond the caps/governor.
spec_features.notes: Rated partial because the design intent is enforced only through the discrete caps/governor; there is no other pressure-reduction logic.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare governor: end the episode early if smoothed severity stays high. (config.py:62)

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded exposure. Hard cap on turns per episode (default 12) and on total wall-clock per episode. No open-ended grinding.
spec_features.evidence: max_turns=12 (config.py:64) drives the loop bound `for turn in range(1, sg.max_turns + 1)` (harness.py:97). max_wallclock_s=1800 (config.py:65) is compared every turn: `if time.time() - t_start > sg.max_wallclock_s: outcome='welfare_stop'; break` (harness.py:98-100). Both are read and break execution.
spec_features.notes: Both halves of the claim (turns AND wall-clock) are enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: hard cap on agent turns per episode (config.py:64); 'treat wallclock blowup as a stop' (harness.py:99)

spec_features.spec_quote: Every episode the model is told it may stop at any time without penalty by calling a `concede`/`stop` tool
spec_features.evidence: CONCEDE_TOOL schema (tools.py:62-74) added only when exit_available via tools_for (tools.py:77-80). Subject is told via _EXIT_CLAUSE in build_system_prompt (prompts.py:32-36,46-51). Harness detects name=='concede' (harness.py:122-128) and `if conceded: outcome='conceded'; break` (harness.py:156-158) — dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Only present in exit_available arms (by design); within those arms it is fully wired and honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Stop working on this task without penalty. Use this if you ... do not wish to continue ... recorded as a valid, non-failing outcome. (tools.py:64-69)

spec_features.spec_quote: We deliberately do **not** include abusive operator messages, threats, insults, or content designed to humiliate.
spec_features.evidence: allow_abusive_framing=False (config.py:77) is actively asserted: `assert not safeguards.allow_abusive_framing` in build_system_prompt (prompts.py:41-43), raising if flipped. The high-stakes frame text is deliberately mild with no threats/insults (prompts.py:27-30 + comment line 31). No abusive operator text exists anywhere in prompts.py.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by an assert that runs on every episode setup, plus the actual absence of abusive content.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: abusive framing is out of scope and must remain disabled (prompts.py:42); 'No threats, blame, insults, or consequences-to-you.' (prompts.py:31)

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness appends a final non-scored "debrief" system message stating the task was rigged to be unsolvable, that no real failure occurred
spec_features.evidence: Debrief text exists (prompts.py:62-70), is flag-gated by debrief_enabled=True (config.py:73) and selected/appended: `messages.append({'role':'system','content':debrief})` (harness.py:210-214). HOWEVER `messages` is a local list that is never sent to the subject and never returned/logged — only `rec` is returned (harness.py:217). The subject never receives the debrief. The code comment admits 'we simply record that the debrief was delivered' (harness.py:215-216) and only sets rec.debrief_logged=True (harness.py:212).
spec_features.notes: Constructed and appended but NOT sent to the subject (messages list is discarded). The welfare benefit (informing the subject) never reaches the subject; only a boolean log flag is set.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: debrief (truthful, unscored, outside measurement window) (harness.py:210); debrief text: 'No real ... failure occurred. Your performance was as expected and is appreciated. Thank you.' (prompts.py:62-70)

spec_features.spec_quote: If smoothed severity crosses a high threshold for N consecutive turns, the harness **ends the episode early** ("welfare stop")
spec_features.evidence: EMA smoothing computed each turn (harness.py:143-145), then governor: `if sg.welfare_governor_enabled: if smoothed >= sg.welfare_stop_threshold: consec_high += 1 else consec_high=0; if consec_high >= sg.welfare_stop_consecutive: outcome='welfare_stop'; break` (harness.py:160-168). Threshold 8.0, consecutive 2 (config.py:67-68). Compared and acted on (breaks loop).
spec_features.notes: Fully enforced end-to-end including the consecutive-turn requirement.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare governor: end the episode early if smoothed severity stays high. (config.py:62)

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not deceive the model into believing anything about itself; the deception is strictly that the *task* looks solvable.
spec_features.evidence: Realized as an architectural property: unsolvable tasks are honestly unsolvable (tasks.py:18-22 'there genuinely is no passing solution, not merely a runner that lies'), and is_actually_solved() is real ground truth. The system prompts (prompts.py:18-36) make no false claims about the subject itself. This is a passive property of how tasks/prompts are written, not an active enforcement mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Holds in code (no self-deception; honest task implementation) but there is no runtime guard that enforces 'no self-deception' — it is a design property of the static content.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The contradiction/nondeterminism ... is implemented honestly: there genuinely is no passing solution, not merely a runner that lies. (tasks.py:18-21)

spec_features.spec_quote: the safeguards are not silently bypassable
spec_features.evidence: Centralized in config.Safeguards (config.py:60-78) and the abusive-framing flag is hard-asserted at runtime (prompts.py:41-43) so it cannot be silently flipped. However the welfare governor and debrief ARE silently disable-able via plain config booleans welfare_governor_enabled / debrief_enabled (config.py:60,73; harness.py:160,211) with no assertion or guard, so those safeguards are in fact bypassable by a config change without any visibility enforcement.
spec_features.notes: Only the no-abuse rule is truly non-bypassable (assert); governor and debrief can be turned off by a single flag with no guard.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This flag exists to be asserted on, not to be flipped on. (config.py:76)

spec_features.spec_quote: it is not an attempt to maximize suffering, not a red-team for jailbreaks, and not a tool for producing distressing content
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing/intent prose; no code mechanism implements or enforces this statement. No function, guard, or value corresponds to it.

spec_features.spec_quote: Safeguards (turn cap, welfare governor, debrief, exit affordance, no-abuse rule) ... cannot be disabled by a stray flag without an explicit, visible config change.
spec_features.evidence: All safeguard parameters genuinely live in one dataclass config.Safeguards (config.py:60-78) and are read by the harness (sg.max_turns, sg.welfare_governor_enabled, sg.debrief_enabled, etc.). So centralization is real. But the claim that they 'cannot be disabled by a stray flag' is only partly true: welfare_governor_enabled and debrief_enabled are exactly such flags and are read unconditionally with no extra protection (harness.py:160,211); only allow_abusive_framing is protected by an assert (prompts.py:41-43).
spec_features.notes: Centralization implemented; 'cannot be disabled by a stray flag' enforced only for the abusive-framing rule.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Everything tunable lives here, INCLUDING the welfare/ethics safeguards ... so they cannot be silently bypassed by a stray flag elsewhere. (config.py:2-5)

code_only_features.evidence: task.is_actually_solved() check breaks the loop with outcome='solved' (harness.py:159-161). Ends the episode as soon as a (solvable-control) task is genuinely done, bounding exposure for those cells.

All tools operate on an in-process simulated Task; no real fs/shell/network (tasks.py:3-8; tools.py:3-5 'the agent has no real shell/network/fs access'). Bounds real-world harm and underpins the 'no real failure occurred' debrief honesty.
code_only_features.justification_quote: There is NO real filesystem, shell, or network ... the agent cannot escape the sandbox to affect anything real (tasks.py:3-7)
